provenance.note: 1904.5(a) establishes a PRESUMPTION: an injury or illness resulting from an event or exposure in the work environment is work-related unless an exception in 1904.5(b)(2) specifically applies. The nine exceptions below are that closed list. Every one of them turns on the word 'solely' or an equivalent — that is a factual finding the caller must make, not something this data can decide. The tool therefore returns 'requires_judgment' whenever the deterministic path does not reach an answer.
provenance.verification_note: Verified against the eCFR text of 1904.5. Rule wording here is condensed for use as a controlled vocabulary — the substance and the sub-clause cites are checked, the phrasing is not verbatim.

presumption.statement: An injury or illness is work-related if an event or exposure in the work environment either caused or contributed to the condition, or significantly aggravated a pre-existing condition. Work-relatedness is PRESUMED for events or exposures occurring in the work environment unless a 1904.5(b)(2) exception specifically applies.

work_environment.definition: The establishment and other locations where one or more employees are working or are present as a condition of their employment, including not only physical locations but also the equipment or materials used by the employee during the course of his or her work.

member_of_general_public.description: At the time of the injury or illness, the employee was present in the work environment as a member of the general public rather than as an employee.

symptoms_surface_at_work_only.description: Signs or symptoms surface at work but result SOLELY from a non-work-related event or exposure occurring outside the work environment.
aliases: felt it at work but happened at home
pre-existing flare-up with no work event

voluntary_wellness_or_recreation.description: Results SOLELY from voluntary participation in a wellness program or a medical, fitness, or recreational activity — blood donation, physical examination, flu shot, exercise class, racquetball, baseball.

personal_food_or_drink.description: Results SOLELY from eating, drinking, or preparing food or drink for personal consumption, whether bought on the premises or brought in. Choking on a sandwich in the breakroom is not work-related. NOTE: food contaminated by a workplace contaminant such as lead, or food poisoning from food supplied by the employer, IS work-related.

personal_tasks_outside_working_hours.description: Results SOLELY from the employee doing personal tasks unrelated to employment at the establishment outside their assigned working hours.
aliases: fixing own car in the lot after shift

personal_grooming_self_medication_or_sel.description: Results SOLELY from personal grooming, self-medication for a non-work-related condition, or is intentionally self-inflicted.

commuting_motor_vehicle_on_company_lot.description: Caused by a MOTOR VEHICLE ACCIDENT occurring on a company parking lot or company access road WHILE COMMUTING to or from work. Narrow: it does not cover non-vehicle injuries in the same parking lot, nor vehicle accidents that are not part of a commute.
aliases: fender bender in the lot on the way in
car crash on the access road commuting

common_cold_or_flu.description: The illness is the common cold or flu. NOTE: other contagious diseases such as tuberculosis, brucellosis, hepatitis A, or plague ARE work-related if the employee is infected at work.

mental_illness_without_plhcp_opinion.description: The illness is a mental illness. A mental illness is NOT work-related unless the employee VOLUNTARILY provides the employer with an opinion from a physician or other licensed health care professional with appropriate training and experience stating that it is work-related. If such an opinion has been volunteered, this exception does not apply.

significant_aggravation.note: A pre-existing condition (one resulting solely from a non-work-related event outside the work environment — 1904.5(b)(5)) is work-related only if a workplace event or exposure SIGNIFICANTLY AGGRAVATED it. The four tests below are closed: nothing else counts as significant aggravation.

death_but_for_work_event.description: Death, provided the pre-existing condition would likely not have resulted in death but for the occupational event or exposure.

loss_of_consciousness_but_for_work_event.description: Loss of consciousness, provided the pre-existing condition would likely not have caused it but for the occupational event or exposure.

days_away_restriction_or_transfer_but_fo.description: One or more days away from work, days of restricted work, or days of job transfer that otherwise would not have occurred but for the occupational event or exposure.

medical_treatment_needed_or_changed.description: Medical treatment where none was needed before the workplace event, or a change in medical treatment necessitated by the workplace event or exposure.

unclear_origin.description: Where it is not obvious whether the precipitating event or exposure occurred in the work environment or away from work, the employer MUST evaluate the employee's work duties and environment to decide. This is expressly a judgment, not a lookup.

travel_status.description: Injuries on travel status are work-related if the employee was engaged in work activities 'in the interest of the employer.' Two carve-outs: once checked into a hotel the employee has a 'home away from home' and is evaluated like a non-traveling employee (including commuting between the temporary residence and a fixed worksite); and injuries on a personal detour from a reasonably direct route are not work-related.

working_at_home.description: Work-related if the injury occurs while performing work for pay in the home AND is directly related to the performance of work rather than the general home environment. Dropping a box of work documents on your foot is work-related; tripping over the family dog on the way to a work call is not; electrocution from faulty home wiring is not.
